headline: Price sits on 734K BTC of new buyers' cost at $80–82K and STH-SOPR slips below 1; a $110M ETF inflow does not yet reverse weak spot demand.
summary: The largest batch of new coins since June ($80–82K, about 734K BTC, estimate) sits right at price, and STH-SOPR at 0.9997 dipped below 1 for the first time, so these buyers have begun exiting at cost. Held, it is the absorbing layer; lost, short-term supply is thin from $76K down to $66K. Bull day 19, no exit rule triggered; watch the FOMC at 02:00 Taipei Oct 29 (18:00 UTC Oct 28) and the Oct 30 monthly expiry.

findings.title: Price sits on new $80–82K supply; below $76K the book thins
findings.lean_why: The thickest new supply is right at price and has started selling at cost while long-term holders distribute; if it fails, thin short-term supply below lets price move fast.
findings.what: Question: with price back at $80–82K, will this bucket's new buyers absorb or sell? The $80,801 close sits in the thickest short-term holder bucket, $80–82K (about 734K BTC, estimate, URPD Oct 26), only +1.68% above the true market mean of $79,468 (this level signal has run 6 days); the same day STH-SOPR fell below 1 to 0.9997 (CheckOnChain Oct 27).
findings.why: Participants (estimate, per-UTXO; our estimated STH cost $74,518 vs bitcoin-data's $74,865, −0.46%): short-term holders 3.516M BTC at an average cost of $74,562; long-term holders 14.289M BTC at $55,010. Two points in time (Sep 20 → Oct 26): of the 3.622M short-term coins then, 1.084M moved, 404K aged into long-term and 2.135M stayed put; long-term holders moved 589K; 1.382M were newly bought and are still unmoved, most at the $80K bucket (606K), $82K (416K) and $84K (269K). So supply has changed hands into $80–86K and short-term cost rose about $2,700 in 30 days. Model-free fact (price never traded there): trapped supply above $88K fell from 4.054M to 3.830M BTC, a real 225K BTC sold. Behavior check: STH-SOPR fell below 1, yet smoothed realized profit of 5,042 BTC is still 2.48× the 2,034 BTC loss (CheckOnChain Oct 27); LTH 30-day net position −199,687 BTC (bitcoin-data Oct 26) and exchange supply 7d +0.48% show long-term holders distributing, consistent with the shrinking trapped supply; the only buyer signal is the Oct 26 provisional ETF +$110M, while the Coinbase premium is still −0.136%.
findings.alt: Part of the 734K BTC at $80–82K comes from the 209K BTC suspected internal transfer on Oct 22 (the model puts those coins back at their original cost and age, but the correction itself is an estimate); per-UTXO data counts exchange wallet consolidation as turnover, overstating it. URPD lags 1 day (Oct 26), and the LTH net position is bitcoin-data's measure, not netted against our estimate. Paper losses do not mean selling.
findings.history: The brief has no historical samples of 'price on the thickest new supply + SOPR just below 1'; the last three STH-SOPR loss lows were all near $62K (Jul 13 0.9762, Aug 1 0.9936, Aug 14 0.9946), when the cost bucket was $62–66K; today's thickest bucket has moved up to $80–82K. Too few samples; background only.
findings.so: Scenarios (conditional): at a $80,000 close about 1.51M short-term and 5.18M long-term coins would be at a paper loss; at $78,000 short-term rises to 1.81M, at $76,000 to 2.12M; further down to $66,000 short-term only reaches 2.24M, so $76K–66K is thin for short-term supply; it jumps to 2.76M only at $64,000 (the June-low buyers at $62–66K). Logic chain: supply has already rotated into $80–86K, so price is now the new buyers' cost defense; they have started exiting at cost while long-term holders distribute, but the loss depth is still shallow, so 'defense broken' is not yet established. Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 3 (covering the FOMC, monthly expiry and midterms): short-term realized loss above 2,500 BTC would mean this new supply is capitulating and confirm the defense is loosening; a close above $82,000 (top of the $80–82K bucket) would put new buyers back in profit and refute this bearish read.

findings.title: Short-term buyers take first loss at cost, far shallower than July
findings.lean_why: Falling below cost in a bull market leans bearish, but the depth is only 0.03% and realized profit is still 2.5× loss, so the signals are mixed.
findings.what: STH-SOPR fell from 1.0014 (Oct 26) to 0.9997 (Oct 27, CheckOnChain daily), its first dip below 1 since the Aug 14 loss low; the same day smoothed short-term realized profit was 5,042 BTC and loss 2,034 BTC, a ratio of 2.48.
findings.why: Breakdown: versus 7 days ago (Oct 20), realized profit +90.1% (2,653 → 5,042) and realized loss +28.5% (1,582 → 2,034); both rose, mostly profit taking. SOPR is a value-weighted daily print while realized P/L is a smoothed coin count; their disagreement suggests the loss-taking is concentrated in the last day or two and has not yet entered the smoothed series. Cross-check: short-term holders in profit 51.63% (Oct 26; 30-day low 49.06%), so about half are under water; net realized P/L on Oct 26 was +$148.9M (CoinMetrics), so the network is still net in profit.
findings.alt: 0.9997 is just 0.03% below 1 and a single-day print, possibly one intraday selling wave; CheckOnChain lags about a day and the daily series averages intraday loss and profit selling. The Oct 20 baseline for the 7-day comparison is also affected by the swings around the Oct 22 transfer day.
findings.history: Last three loss lows: Jul 13 0.9762 (11 days below 1, deeper than Jun 25), Aug 1 0.9936 (6 days, easing), Aug 14 0.9946 (8 days, easing); only 3 samples, background only. Today's depth is shallower than all three.
findings.so: The prior read 'profit taking into the drop, not panic selling' is refuted by SOPR dropping below 1 (see follow-ups); but so far this is shallow loss-taking at cost, not capitulation. Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Oct 31: STH-SOPR below 0.99 (deeper than both August lows) would mean heavier losses and refute the 'shallow loss' read; back above 1 would confirm it was brief selling at cost.

items.title: Quantifying Support and Resistance: Proximity-Weighted CBD
items.points: Weights the cost-basis distribution by distance from spot; when PSI (weighted share of supply below spot) rises above 50%, support dominates; in Apr–May 2026 an 83.6K–85.4K resistance band formed before price fell to the low 60Ks; related October posts treat 85K–87.5K as resistance and ~80K as support.
items.meaning: Methodology research; compare with our ±5% supply concentration of 14.87% and the supply pile at $80–86K; we don't apply its thresholds.

items.title: Perpetual Preferred Stock: The Newest Demand Catalyst for Bitcoin
items.points: Perpetual preferreds have funded 135,979 BTC of corporate buying since 2025-07 (to Oct 5, over 0.5% of supply), more than 95,000 BTC in March–May alone with over $7B raised; it works only while BTC's gains exceed the dividend cost.
items.meaning: Strategy buying back STRC instead of bitcoin last week confirms this demand channel is slowing; consistent with the spot absence in the site's Coinbase premium, and not used for the cycle call.
